subject: Prod traffic bounceback after rate plan cutover — HealthLink 429 wave
messages:
From: Samir Desai <samir@healthlink.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-09T22:12:00-08:00
Subject: Spike in 429s after rate plan cutover — urgent

Tessa —

We just finished the rate plan cutover for our project (healthlink-prod) at ~21:50 PST and immediately started seeing a large spike of 429s and client-side timeouts. Traffic looks like normal volume but a large fraction of requests are being rejected with 429 or timing out after retries. This started ~10 minutes after the cutover and is still ongoing. Our engineers are seeing retry storms and downstream service errors.

Attached are a short sample of logs and a traffic chart showing the bounceback pattern.

What we need: immediate mitigation — reduce user-facing errors. Can you confirm whether the rollout changed org/project tier mapping or quota assignments? We are seeing headers that indicate rate_limit: project_quota_exceeded for many requests.

We are on a tight maintenance window and this is user-impacting — please escalate.

— Samir
Ops, HealthLink
(attachment: healthlink-429-sample-logs.txt, traffic-bounce-chart.png)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Desai <samir@healthlink.com>
Date: 2027-01-09T22:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 429s after rate plan cutover — urgent

Folks —

Observed same 429 pattern in our monitoring. Initial triage: the rate plan cutover job updated project->tier mappings for HealthLink (project id: HL-prod-42) at 21:49 PST; an incorrect mapping pushed the project into a lower-rate tier that has much tighter org-level and project-level quotas. That explains the immediate wave of quota_exceeded 429s and the retry amplification.

Immediate actions proposed (I started them):
- Opened incident PD-91234 and tagged platform-oncall.
- Asked infra to temporarily increase the project quota and loosen burst limits for HL-prod-42 (pending approval).
- Preparing an emergency rollback of the mapping to the previous tier.
- Advising HealthLink to pause aggressive client retries for 10 minutes (Samir, please confirm).

Can Marissa/Rishi approve: (1) emergency quota bump to match previous tier for 1 hour, (2) rollback the tier mapping to the pre-cutover state while we fix the deploy rule. If approved I will execute the rollback and coordinate comms with HealthLink.

Attachments: runbook-revert-playbook.pdf (I referenced the revert steps)

— Tessa
Redwood — Technical Account Manager

Subject: Re: Spike in 429s after rate plan cutover — urgent

Team — executive summary for leadership: HealthLink production experienced a sudden 429 surge after an automated rateplan cutover pushed their project into a lower-rate tier. This is a config/deploy-mapping error, not a model performance regression. Customer impact: elevated 5xx/429 rates, increased latency from retry storms, user-visible errors for search & document ingestion.

Decision requested (please reply ALL):
1) Approve emergency quota bump: restore project quotas to the previous tier levels for 60 minutes (rollback window).
2) Approve immediate rollback of the new mapping to the prior mapping for HL-prod-42.
3) If rollback completes, authorize a short cooling window where HealthLink will delay retries by 60s to avoid congestion.

Risk: small additional cost for the hour of elevated quota. Benefit: will stop the retry amplification and allow a clean, corrected redeploy of mapping rules.

If I do not hear objections in 10 minutes I will proceed with the quota bump + mapping rollback.

-- Marissa
VP, Customer Success Operations

Date: 2027-01-10T03:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 429s after rate plan cutover — urgent

Marissa/Team —

Approved. Actions executed at 03:15 PST:
- Rolled back project->tier mapping for HL-prod-42 to pre-cutover mapping (deployment tag: rollback-20270109-2145).
- Applied temporary quota increase to match previous tier limits for 60 minutes.
- Enabled a short, per-project burst allowance to avoid additional 429 spikes while caches warm.

Monitoring: 429 rate dropped from ~18% to ~0.8% within 7 minutes after rollback; overall latency back to baseline by 03:30 PST. HealthLink confirmed client retries have paused per our request.

Next steps:
- Postmortem scheduled for 2027-01-11 10:00 PST (owner: Neha).
- Action item: add pre-cutover validation for tier-mapping jobs and a dry-run that checks projected quota allocation.
- Follow-up: update the deployment job to prevent silent mapping downgrades (PR #PLT-485).

Attachments: traffic-bounce-chart.png, healthlink-429-sample-logs.txt

Thanks — Rishi
Director, Platform Reliability
